Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: normal hours, overtime limit, warning days, days to pay a subcontractor, pass mark for inductions and the late payment interest.
Fill Projects and Trade Rates first. Trade Rates holds the wage, on-costs, overtime factor and agency day rate for each trade.
Add every subcontractor on Subcontractors, then each order on Subcontract Packages with its value, retention rate and dates.
Record every monthly application on Payment Applications: type the work done to date and what you paid before. Retention, the payment due, days open, status and late interest fill in.
Log variations on Subcontract Variations, documents on Compliance Documents and reviews on Performance Ratings. Each subcontractor shows its status on Subcontractors.
Add your own workers on Workers and your gangs on Crews and Gangs. The loaded hour comes from the trade rate.
Type one row on Timesheets for each worker and week with the project, normal hours and overtime hours. Cost and the overtime limit check fill in.
Record Overtime Log, Attendance and Absence, Training and Certificates, Site Induction Records and Tools and PPE Issued as they happen.
Measure output on Labour Productivity, list the workers you lack on Labour Shortages and read Labour Cost by Project and Payroll Summary each month.

Use the 14 calculators for subcontract payments, retention, expiry, hourly cost, crew size, productivity, overtime, own or subcontract, accrual, utilisation, absence, piece rates, agency or hire and payment dates.
Read the Labour and Subs Dashboard and Charts every week: overdue applications, ended documents, overtime, absence, shortages and projects over budget.
Claim every month, collect retention and see the cash gap coming
Claim every month, collect retention, see the cash gap
every part of the work shows the share done before and now; the claim adds variations, takes off retention and advance recovery and gives the net to invoice
money owed is split into not yet due, 30, 60, 90 and over 90 days late for every client, with a status that warns early
retention to date, released and held, with the first and final release dates from practical completion and the defects period
Under and over billing by project
billing is compared with the work your site team measured, so you see money you can claim and money you hold that is not yet earned
each certificate shows the cut from your claim, the days the client took and a flag for reductions you should challenge
interest on money still owed and on payments already received late, ready to invoice after your grace days
new claims arrive after your payment lag, retention comes back on its dates and open invoices fall due; the closing balance shows the months below your floor
the share of every claim that repays the advance, with the amount recovered and the balance to recover for each project
every call and message is logged with the date the client promised to pay, and broken promises are flagged
final value, still to bill and cash still to collect for each contract, with the bonds and guarantees that must stay valid until the end

Project billing: contract, claims, money in, work done
One row for each contract with its value, retention and the share of work your site team measured; revised value, billed, received, retention held, outstanding and over or under billing fill in.
Clients with payment terms and how they really pay
One row for each client with the days they have to pay, the days they take to certify and the interest rate for late payment; claims, received, outstanding, days late and a payer rating fill in.
Schedule of values for each contract
One row for each part of a contract with its value; the share done to date, the value earned and the value left fill in from the claim lines.
Progress claims, retention and money still owed
One row for each monthly claim; work, variations, gross, retention, advance recovery, net, certified, received, outstanding, due date, days overdue and status fill in.
Claim lines: percent complete times value
One row for each part of the work in a claim with the share done before and in this period; project, value, share to date, value this period and value to date fill in.
One row for each variation with the claim it is in, its reason, amount and whether the client approved it; only approved variations are added to the claim.
Payment certificates and what they cut
One row for each certificate the client sends with the amount certified; the amount claimed, the cut, the days the client took and a flag for cuts you should challenge fill in.
Client payments with days late and interest
One row for each payment received; project, client, due date, days late, days the client took and the late payment interest you can charge fill in.
Receivables ageing by client: what is owed and how old it is
One row for each client; the amounts not yet due and overdue by 30, 60, 90 and over 90 days, the total owed and a status fill in from the claims.
Retention held by clients and release dates
One row for each contract with its practical completion date and defects months; retention to date, released, balance, release dates and a status fill in.
One row for each release of retention you receive, with its date, amount and kind; project and month fill in and the balance held updates.
Advance payments and how they are recovered
One row for each advance with the share recovered from every claim; recovered so far, the balance still to recover and a status fill in.
Supplier, subcontractor and hire invoices you still owe
One row for each invoice you receive with its terms and the date you paid; due date, amount still open, days overdue and a status fill in.
Cash flow forecast for the next 12 months
One row for each month: type what you expect to collect, bill and spend; money from new claims, retention and open invoices, the net, the closing balance and a warning below your floor fill in.
Bank balance log: one line a week
One row each week with the bank balance; the month, the distance from your floor and a status fill in.
Overdue claims follow-up: every call, message and promise
One row for each time you chase a client about a claim, with the outcome and the date the client promised to pay; the amount still owed, days overdue and whether the promise was kept fill in.
Disputed amounts and how they end
One row for each dispute with the amount, the reason and the date it was settled; the amount still open, the money lost, the age and a status fill in.
Final accounts: the last claim and what is still to collect
One row for each contract near its end with the omissions and extras you agree; final value, billed, still to bill, cash still to collect and the status fill in.
Bonds, guarantees and insurance with their end dates
One row for each bond, guarantee or insurance with provider, amount, dates and premium rate; days left, premium and a warning before it ends fill in.
Late payment interest you can charge
One row for each claim paid late or still overdue; the interest on money still owed, the interest on late payments already received, the total and whether you have invoiced it fill in.

Tell a client a claim was sent
Hello, we sent claim {no} for "{proj}". The net amount is {net} and payment is due on {due}. Please tell us when you expect to certify it.
Ask when a claim will be certified
Hello, we are waiting for the certificate for claim {no} of "{proj}", sent on {submitted}. Can you tell us the date?
Remind a client a payment is coming due
Hello, a reminder that {outstanding} for claim {no} of "{proj}" is due on {due}. Please confirm the payment date.
Hello, {outstanding} for claim {no} of "{proj}" is {days_over} days overdue. Please pay it this week or tell us the date.
Ask for the rest after a part payment
Hello, thank you for the part payment on claim {no} of "{proj}". {outstanding} is still unpaid. When will you send the rest?
Ask to discuss a disputed amount
Hello, {disputed} of claim {no} on "{proj}" is in dispute. Can we meet this week with the measurements and settle it?
Ask why a certificate was cut
Hello, the certificate for "{proj}" shows {certified} against our claim of {claimed}. Please send the reasons for the reduction of {cut}.
Hello, we received the certificate for "{proj}" for {certified}. We confirm it and send our invoice today.
Thank a client for a payment
Hello, we received {amount} on {date}, reference {ref}. Thank you for your payment.
Tell a client about late interest
Hello, your payment of {amount} arrived {days_late} days after the due date. Interest of {interest} applies under the contract. We will send the invoice.
Ask a client to clear the balance
Hello {name}, your balance with us is {total}, of which {b30} is 1 to 30 days late. Please pay the overdue part this week.
Warn about money over 90 days late
Hello {name}, {b90p} has been unpaid for more than 90 days. Please call us today so that we can agree a payment plan.
Remind a client of the payment terms
Hello {name}, our contract gives {pay_days} days to pay each claim and {cert_days} days to certify it. Please help us keep to these dates.
Hello, for "{name}" we have billed {billed}, you have paid {received} and {outstanding} is outstanding. Retention held is {held}.
Agree the work done before a claim
Hello, before our next claim for "{name}" we would like to agree the work done, now {progress} by our measure. When can we walk the site together?
Hello, variations of {vo} are approved on "{name}". Please approve the pending ones so that we can include them in the next claim.
Ask for retention to be released
Hello, the retention release for "{proj}" fell due on {first_date}. The balance held is {balance}. Please release it.
Remind a client defects end soon
Hello, the defects period of "{proj}" ends on {final_date}. Please send us any defect before then so that the final retention can be released.
Remind a client of a promise
Hello, you promised to pay {owed} for "{proj}" by {promise}. Please confirm that the payment is on its way.
Ask a client to call back
Hello, we tried to reach you about {owed} owed on "{proj}", now {days_over} days overdue. Please call us today.
Hello, the dispute of {amount} on "{proj}" has been open for {age} days. Can we agree the settlement this week?
Hello, we send the measurements and instructions for the disputed {amount} on "{proj}". Please review them before our meeting.
Hello, we send the final account of "{proj}". The final value is {final_value} and {cash_due} is still to collect, with retention. Please confirm it.
Ask to agree the final account
Hello, the final account of "{proj}" was due to be agreed by {submit_by}. Can we meet this week to close it?
Hello, our {type} for "{proj}" ends on {expiry}. Please send the renewal terms and the premium this week.
Tell a payee when they will be paid
Hello {payee}, invoice {ap_id} for {amount} is due on {due}. We will pay it on that date.
Hello {payee}, we are sorry that invoice {ap_id} for {amount} is {days_over} days late. We will pay it this week.
Hello {payee}, please send a credit note for invoice {ap_id} of {amount}. We found a difference in the delivery.
Tell a client about interest due
Hello, interest of {total} is due on late payments for "{proj}". We will send the invoice. Please include it in your next payment.
Cover letter for a progress claim
Project: {col:claims.proj}. Claim number {col:claims.no}, for the period ending {col:claims.period}.
We submit our claim for the work done in the period. The work done is {col:claims.work} and the approved variations are {col:claims.vo}, making a gross claim of {col:claims.gross}.
After retention of {col:claims.ret} and advance recovery of {col:claims.adv}, the net amount to certify and pay is {col:claims.net}. Payment is due on {col:claims.due}.
The detailed lines and the percent complete of each part of the work are attached. Please send your certificate within the time stated in the contract.
Our records show that {col:claims.outstanding} is still unpaid on this claim. It was due on {col:claims.due} and is now {col:claims.days_over} days overdue.
Please pay the amount this week or tell us the date on which you will pay. If anything in the claim is in question, tell us which part so that we can settle the rest.
We reserve our right to charge interest on late payment under the contract.
Under the payment terms of the contract we charge interest on money paid late. The interest on payments already received and on the amount still owed comes to {col:interest.total}.
The amount still owed is {col:interest.owed}, now {col:interest.days_over} days overdue, at a yearly rate of {col:interest.rate}.
Please include the interest in your next payment. Tell us if you wish to discuss it.
We claimed {col:certs.claimed} net and the certificate shows {col:certs.certified}. The difference is {col:certs.cut}.
Please send the reasons for the reduction and the measurements behind it, line by line. We will check them and reply within five working days.
Until the reasons are agreed, we ask you to pay the amount that is not in question.
Retention held to date is {col:ret.retained}, of which {col:ret.released} has been released. The balance held is {col:ret.balance}.
The first release is due on {col:ret.first_date} and the final release on {col:ret.final_date}, at the end of the defects period of {col:ret.defects_m} months.
Please release the amount that has fallen due and confirm the date of payment.
We record a dispute of {col:disp.amount} raised on {col:disp.raised}. The reason is: {col:disp.reason}.
We propose to meet within ten days with the measurements and the contract clauses, and to agree the amount to be paid.
The undisputed part of the claim must be paid on its due date.
This cover ends on {col:bonds.expiry}. We ask you to send the renewal terms and the premium, and the new certificate before that date.
The cover must continue without a break until the contract allows it to end.

The contract value was {col:final.contract}, with approved variations of {col:final.vo}, omissions of {col:final.omissions} and extras of {col:final.extras}. The final value is {col:final.final_value}.
We have billed {col:final.billed} and received {col:final.received}. After the advance of {col:final.advance}, the cash still to collect, including retention, is {col:final.cash_due}.
Please check the account and confirm it in writing so that the retention can be released.
We confirm that we received {col:pays.amount} on {col:pays.date} against claim {col:pays.claim}, reference {col:pays.ref}.
The payment was due on {col:pays.due}. It arrived {col:pays.days_late} days after the due date.
Late payment interest of {col:pays.interest} applies under the contract. Thank you for your payment.
Statement of an advance payment and its recovery
Project: {col:adv.proj}. Advance received on {col:adv.received}: {col:adv.amount}, under guarantee {col:adv.guarantee}.
We recover {col:adv.rec_pct} of every gross claim. Recovered so far: {col:adv.recovered}. Still to recover: {col:adv.balance}.
The guarantee will be reduced as the advance is recovered. Please confirm this statement.
